issues.description: The UML and problem description specify numberOfLecturers as an int attribute, but the solution implementation declares numberOfLecturers as a byte. This type mismatch between the specification and the provided solution can confuse students about the expected type and lead to incompatible constructor/setter signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution's numberOfLecturers field type from byte to int to match the UML and problem statement. Update any related code (constructor parameter, setter parameter) to use int as well.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and instructions expect the constructor to initialize attributes in the order and types shown (lectureName: String, numberOfInscribedStudents: int, numberOfGuestStudents: int, numberOfLecturers: int, numberOfTutors: int). The solution's constructor uses a byte parameter for numberOfLecturers, which conflicts with the expected int type.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the constructor parameter type for numberOfLecturers from byte to int so it matches the UML and problem description. Ensure the parameter order remains as specified in the UML.

issues.description: The setter for numberOfLecturers in the solution accepts a byte parameter (setNumberOfLecturers(byte ...)), while the UML and problem tasks imply an int type for this attribute and its setter. This parameter type mismatch can confuse students and may not match test expectations derived from the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the setter signature to setNumberOfLecturers(int numberOfLecturers) and update its implementation accordingly so the method parameter type matches the UML-specified int.
